title: Euro Slides to 17-Month Low on Eurozone Political and Fiscal Risks
summary: Gotrade News - The euro slid to its lowest level in roughly 17 months against the US dollar, falling below $1.13 for the first time since May 2025 as
body_markdown:
## Eurozone Inflation at 3.8% Complicates the ECB Outlook


The energy shock is feeding directly into prices. According to[Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/euro-area/currency/news/585569) , eurozone inflation accelerated to 3.8%, its highest since September 2023 and well above the European Central Bank's 2% target, driven largely by higher fuel prices.

## Dollar Strength and What It Means for US Stocks


The other side of the trade is a firm greenback. As reported by Reuters via GBM, the Dollar Index rose 0.31% to near its highest level since mid-May 2025, and the dollar posted a sixth consecutive quarterly gain, its longest streak since 2022, as[US Treasury yields](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/rising-bond-yields-dollar-strength-fed-rate-hike-bets/) recorded their biggest quarterly increase since 1994.


That support softened on Friday's data. Per Trading Economics, the US economy added just 29,000 jobs in September, well below expectations of 90,000, lifting bets that the Fed may hold rates at its upcoming meeting. The[weak jobs report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/jobs-report-tests-stocks-after-yield-spike/) helped the euro bounce off its lows.


For investors in US stocks, a weaker euro means euro-denominated revenue converts into fewer dollars. That is a factor to watch for US multinationals with large European sales, such as[McDonald's (MCD)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/mcd/) ,[Coca-Cola (KO)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/ko/) , and[Procter & Gamble (PG)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/pg/) , when they report results.
